messages:
Leah (Solutions Eng): Hey all — Acme trial keeps hitting a 413 when they send long chat histories. Happens on /v1/generate when they include full convo + system prompt (~120k chars). Error returns: `413 Payload Too Large`. Can anyone share quick mitigations?
Sam (AE): Which model/context window are they targeting?
Leah (Solutions Eng): They picked redwood-32k-v1 but client is bundling entire org chat history into one request. Client says they need "full context" for accuracy.
Mina (MLEng): Sending 120k chars in one request is rough. Our gateway limit for hosted tier is ~200KB by default (Content-Length cap). If compressed it might fit, but streaming/partial requests are better.
Leah (Solutions Eng): They get immediate 413 from gateway; no model error. Customer asked if we can "just raise it" for the POC.
Oliver (DevEx): Short-term options: 1) enable gzip on client and set Content-Encoding: gzip; 2) use prefix caching + only send last N turns; 3) split history and perform reranking/embedding search server-side then send top-k. Example curl for gzip: 
```
cat payload.json | gzip -c > payload.json.gz
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Encoding: gzip" \
  --data-binary @payload.json.gz
```
Leah (Solutions Eng): Good — they want a code sample for auto-trimming too. Any snippet for conv trimming?
Mina (MLEng): Keep last ~2-4 turns + a short system summary. Pseudocode: 
```
function trim_conversation(conv, max_tokens) {
  // summarize earlier turns or drop older ones
  while(token_count(conv) > max_tokens) { drop_oldest_user_assistant_pair(conv) }
  return conv
}
```
Sam (AE): On the policy side — we can do a temporary hosted gateway bump for an eval but need approvals. Will that create cost impact for them?
Leah (Solutions Eng): They asked whether Dedicated would avoid this entirely.
Mina (MLEng): Dedicated gives higher configured limits and you can tune the ingress/proxy. But usually you still want to avoid sending enormous request bodies because of latency and model context inefficiency.
Sam (AE): For the POC we can offer a 48h increase for org-acme if infra approves. I'll start the approval with Sales Ops.
DeployBot: infra: request received to increase body_limit for org-acme. Temp change scheduled: +24h pending oncall approval. (note: change not applied yet)
Oliver (DevEx): Also remind them about max_tokens param — if model is 32k window but they request full history, model will still truncate to fit context. So they may be sending redundant text. Recommend embeddings search: store convo as embeddings, fetch top-k relevant chunks, then send those.
Leah (Solutions Eng): Customer also worried about pricing if we enable temp increase. Sam, can you confirm billing?
Sam (AE): Temporary increase won't alter pricing in billing UI, but prolonged high token usage will. I'll add a note in the quote: sustained large requests may trigger discussion about Dedicated / reserved capacity.
Mina (MLEng): If they must send large docs, another pattern: upload the large blob to S3 and send a reference token to the model (client does smaller metadata request); we resolve server-side and stream relevant snippets.
Leah (Solutions Eng): I'll send them the gzip + trimming samples, and offer the 24h trial bump while Sam gets approvals. Can someone point to a prod log line I can include?
Oliver (DevEx): Here is a sanitized gateway log example to paste: `2025-11-12T14:12:03Z INFO gateway request_id=abc123 client=10.4.2.3 org=org-acme status=413 content_length=127892 route=/v1/generate`
Leah (Solutions Eng): Perfect. Thanks — looping @Sam and will follow up with the customer. :thumbsup:
Sam (AE): I'll handle approvals and update thread.
DeployBot: infra: oncall approved temporary increase at 1769804500; change applied.
Leah (Solutions Eng): Closing for now, will reopen if 413 reappears after change.
